newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish privatisation board to decide on sell-offs.
newsitem.headline: Turkish privatisation board to decide on sell-offs.

text.p: Turkey's High Board of Privatisation (OYK) will meet on Thursday afternoon to make the final decision on sell-offs of several state-owned plants, ports and banks, officials said.
The companies being privatised include six cement and ceramics factories, one chromium plant, seven ports, one tyre maker and three banks, they said.
The government, which expects to receive $881.7 million from he sale of the companies, has received bids from local investors and has already announced the highest bidders.
The OYK, whose decision is final, is chaired by Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan and includes four other senior ministers.

The government expects to receive $5 to $7 billion from sell-offs this year, including the initial privatisatioin of Turk Telekom, the partial sale of steel maker Eregli, oil refiner Tupras, petroleum marketer Petrol Ofisi, petroleum products producer Petkim and state airliner THY, and some other smaller firms.
